posts.note: Interview transcript with Radial technician Nogga Schwartz about the Soft White Underbelly videos. One social prediction by the author; one third-party (Nogga) statement about pursuing insurance coverage.
Short podcast note plus RAMHT New Orleans (September 14th) event promotion; only own-event announcements, all CONTROL candidates.

Essay on bipolar depression treatment gap and the KET-BD IV ketamine trial. Substantive calls on SNT/accelerated TMS efficacy, FDA label pathway, payer coverage, and market incentives. Kanye West apology letter in footnote is quoted third-party text with no forecasts.

Long interview transcript with Dr. Randy Pardell (Clearwave Mental Health, FACTMS). Most forward-looking statements are Pardell's (own_claim false); the author endorses the SSRI-obsolescence forecast and adds a payer pattern claim and a donation call to action. Many 'I would love' wishes not logged.

Short video note with links; newsletter content promises, RAMHT coverage, and a psychedelic open comment period on September 14th. Link headlines (Radial acquisition, Ampa financing) are past news, not logged.

statements.quote: You were a big hit, so I’m sure you’d be welcome back.
statements.context: Owen (interviewer) to Nogga Schwartz, Radial technician, about Nogga's solo interview on Mark Laita's Soft White Underbelly YouTube channel. Owen predicts Nogga would be invited back to the channel.
statements.note: Social prediction about a return invitation; low forecast value.

statements.quote: There were questions about whether this is covered by insurance, and I went in and answered them myself: that’s something we’re working on.
statements.context: Nogga Schwartz (Radial technician, interviewee) on YouTube comments asking whether the accelerated TMS treatment shown in the Soft White Underbelly video (Ampa One device with D-cycloserine, delivered by Radial) is covered by insurance; he says Radial is working on insurance coverage.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Nogga Schwartz) speaking for Radial, the author's company. Implied claim only: coverage is being pursued, no date. Borderline.

statements.quote: RAMHT New Orleans is coming up on September 14th.
statements.context: Announcement of the RAMHT (author's own event series) New Orleans event at the Historic BK House & Gardens, 5-9pm, with free Eventbrite tickets; sponsors listed include Neurolief and Radial. Post dated 2026-09-01.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: We’ll be sharing more details on speakers, rapid-fire talks and panel discussions on the RAMHT website and LinkedIn page
statements.context: RAMHT New Orleans (September 14th) event announcement; the author promises upcoming details on speakers, rapid-fire talks and panel discussions via the RAMHT website and LinkedIn page.
statements.note: Own-activity content promise; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Also, we will have special guests. And surprises.
statements.context: RAMHT New Orleans event (September 14th) promotion; the author says the event will have special guests and surprises.
statements.note: Own-event detail; CONTROL candidate. Event date September 14th given earlier in the post.

statements.quote: And maybe….just maybe… embarrassing merch, for me, personally.
statements.context: RAMHT New Orleans event (September 14th) promotion; the author hedges that the event may include merchandise embarrassing to him personally.
statements.note: Playful tease but reads as a real hedge; low forecast value; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: I've previously written about the promise of accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation, particularly the SNT approach, in bipolar depression. It does look like that's likely to work
statements.context: Author's own call that accelerated TMS, specifically the SNT (Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy, SAINT) approach, is likely to prove effective for bipolar depression. Set up by a review of the short list of FDA-labeled options for acute bipolar depression (all atypical antipsychotics) and the me-too drug problem.
statements.note: Restatement of an earlier call the author references ('I've previously written'). Efficacy claim; the label-change pathway is logged separately.

statements.quote: somebody has to do a large enough trial, submitted to the FDA, to change the label, and that just starts the conversation with payers about coverage.
statements.context: Continuation of the SNT-in-bipolar-depression point: the author says an FDA label change for accelerated TMS in bipolar depression requires a sufficiently large trial submitted to the FDA, and that a label change only begins the payer coverage conversation, so coverage will lag any label.
statements.note: Conditional pathway claim; 'has to' reads as necessity (no label without a large trial), not advice. Compound: label change plus payer coverage lag.

statements.quote: Today we have more data, that's hopeful, but unlikely to lead to meaningful coverage, because the academic researchers chose to study something. I bring you: IV ketamine. For bipolar depression.
statements.context: The KET-BD randomized trial (IV ketamine vs midazolam, 3 Ontario sites, July 2022 to November 2025) showed a significant MADRS benefit in treatment-resistant bipolar depression; the author forecasts this academic data is unlikely to lead to meaningful payer coverage of IV ketamine for bipolar depression.
statements.note: Negative call on coverage; reasoning given is that an investigator-led study of a generic drug does not move payers.

statements.quote: Bipolar depression is more of an unmeetable need, at least in Pharma and med device—because between two pitches, the founder who promises to go after a market 5x bigger wins, all things being equal.
statements.context: Structural market claim: because the unipolar depression market is about 5x the bipolar market (author cites a $1.7b bipolar estimate), founders will pitch new treatments as MDD products and bipolar depression will stay underserved by pharma and med-device development. Related sentence: 'You're going to say it works for major depressive disorder a.k.a. unipolar depression, instead of bipolar depression.'
statements.note: Ongoing structural claim rather than a dated event; implies continued lack of bipolar-depression-specific development. Borderline.

statements.quote: This will be less true financially than it will be emotionally, but I'm OK with that.
statements.context: Closing pitch to investors: the author says he will tell anyone deciding which company to fund that a company aiming to make a big dent in bipolar disorder is a good idea, then concedes the case is weaker financially than emotionally, i.e., he expects the financial return to be less compelling than the emotional one.
statements.note: Soft forecast about returns on bipolar-focused investment; borderline.

statements.quote: We were just on the phone yesterday talking about how, to your point, we’ll be questioning why we ever did this with SSRIs. We studied them for six weeks and then prescribed them for 20 years.
statements.context: Owen (author), disclosing that he advises Mark Horowitz's company Outro Health and spoke with co-founder Brandon the day before, endorses Randy Pardell's forecast that the field will look back on long-term SSRI prescribing as a mistake.
statements.note: Author's endorsed restatement of Randy Pardell's forecast (Pardell's version logged separately with own_claim false).

statements.quote: Every time TMS has been evaluated, eventually it’s determined that this is a great option and more people should have access to it.
statements.context: Owen's question to Randy Pardell about advice for payers; he characterizes payer and regulator evaluations of TMS as a 'tidal wave of change over many years, all in the direction of more TMS, not less', a universal pattern that implies future TMS evaluations will also end favorably.
statements.note: Generalization from a past pattern; the forward-looking reading is implicit. Borderline.

statements.quote: a donation to the Foundation for the Advancement of Clinical TMS means more people get access to TMS treatment at a lower cost to them, and there’ll be more research supporting the next person who needs it
statements.context: Owen's closing call to action after the interview: donations to FACTMS (the foundation Randy Pardell heads and Carlene MacMillan sits on the board of) will translate into more patient access to TMS at lower cost and more research funding.
entities: Foundation for the Advancement of Clinical TMS
statements.note: Conditional on donations; fundraising call to action; low forecast value.

statements.quote: Now we’re going to be opening our tenth site in Syracuse. ... we’re building out general psychiatry, TMS, and Spravato sites throughout New York State.
statements.context: Randy Pardell (interviewee, Chief Medical Officer of Clearwave Mental Health) on his practice's growth after the COVID pause: Clearwave will open its tenth site, in Syracuse, and is building out general psychiatry, TMS and Spravato sites across New York State.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Randy Pardell); own-business expansion plan.

statements.quote: We currently have eight therapists working with us, soon to be nine, and we’re growing our therapy practice
statements.context: Randy Pardell on Clearwave Mental Health's psychotherapy build-out alongside TMS: eight therapists now, soon nine, and a growing therapy practice.
statements.note: Quoted third party; minor operational forecast.

statements.quote: I think we can be giving TMS much more effectively. ... Making TMS more effective, so that instead of being 60% effective, it’s 90% effective or more.
statements.context: Randy Pardell, asked about the most promising innovations: TMS as a platform can become far more effective through low-cost functional imaging for targeting and stimulating more than one brain spot, raising effectiveness from about 60% to 90% or more.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Randy Pardell). Numeric target: 60% to 90% or more effectiveness; no date.

statements.quote: I do think wearables might be down the road.
statements.context: Randy Pardell on future neuromodulation: wearable at-home devices may come later; he mentions trying a trigeminal and occipital nerve stimulator and app-based approaches as helpful directions.
statements.note: Quoted third party. The unnamed trigeminal and occipital nerve stimulator he describes resembles the Neurolief device (an author-affiliated company); device not named in the text.

statements.quote: The standard monoamine serotonin reuptake inhibitors, the SSRIs, the SNRIs, may actually be in the past. We’ll say, “How did we ever do that?” in the next 10 or 15 years, when we’re doing much more transformational changes with neuromodulation and potentially some of the psychedelic treatments down the line.
statements.context: Randy Pardell forecasts that SSRIs and SNRIs will be seen as obsolete within 10 to 15 years as neuromodulation and possibly psychedelic treatments (his practice offers Spravato) take over. Owen later endorses this ('we'll be questioning why we ever did this with SSRIs').
statements.note: Quoted third party; author endorses later in the post (logged separately as own claim). Compound: SSRIs obsolete plus neuromodulation and psychedelics dominant.

statements.quote: If you can provide that to our insurer colleagues so they can be convinced, you’re going to start to see more and more conditions approved by insurance companies.
statements.context: Randy Pardell's advice to payers: with evidence (RCTs or large registries such as the NeuroStar registry) plus a value case (undertreated patients cost insurers more; accelerated one-to-five-day protocols make treatment observable), insurers will approve TMS for more and more conditions. He names bipolar depression, schizophrenia and hallucinations as hoped-for targets.
statements.confidence_phrase: you’re going to start to see
statements.note: Quoted third party; conditional on evidence and value data being provided to insurers.

statements.quote: Just to let you know, the foundation is having a free webinar next month, on September twenty-ninth. facttms.org is our website. Sam Huber, who is medical director of the neuromodulation program at MVP Health Plan, is going to be one of the guests, I’m going to be one of the guests, and Ian Cook is going to be the moderator.
statements.context: Randy Pardell announces a FACTMS free webinar on September 29 with Sam Huber (MVP Health Plan medical director), himself as guest and Ian Cook as moderator. 'Next month' reflects the recording date; the post is dated 2026-09-04.
entities: Foundation for the Advancement of Clinical TMS
statements.note: Quoted third party; dated event announcement.

statements.quote: We’re going to be redoing our website, having podcasts, having social events, and having our free webinars.
statements.context: Randy Pardell on FACTMS plans to increase awareness of TMS: a new website, podcasts, social events and free webinars.
statements.note: Quoted third party; organizational plans, low forecast value.

statements.quote: I have a multi-part article on the Lindsay Clancy case coming up soon.
statements.context: Author's newsletter plans: a multi-part article on the Lindsay Clancy case is forthcoming in The Frontier Psychiatrists.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: We also have exciting coverage regarding RAMHT New Orleans on September 14th.
statements.context: Author promises newsletter coverage of the RAMHT New Orleans event on September 14th (author's own event series).
statements.note: Own-event and newsletter promise; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: There is a psychedelic open comment period that same day!
statements.context: Author notes that a psychedelic-related regulatory open comment period falls on September 14th, the same day as RAMHT New Orleans; the agency and docket are not named.
statements.note: Regulatory calendar item; agency not named; 'that same day' refers to September 14th. Low forecast value.
